text: Alice proposed PostgreSQL for the payments platform during the architecture discussion.
Bob questioned whether PostgreSQL could handle the payments platform's projected transaction load.
Alice said the benchmark results were inconclusive and asked the team to test PostgreSQL under peak load.
Carol reported that Redis was already being used for session caching in the payments platform.
Bob proposed using Redis for rate limiting, but it was unclear whether he meant the payments platform or a separate service.
Alice reported that the peak-load benchmark completed successfully, although its failover behavior remained uncertain.
Bob said the rate-limiting change might require a different deployment plan.
Carol said the payments platform team planned to keep Redis for caching while they decided on the database changes.
After the failover test, Alice proposed PostgreSQL again, but no final adoption decision was recorded.
Bob and Carol reviewed the architecture document; Bob favored a separate rate-limiting service, while Carol favored keeping Redis for caching.
